doc.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Planned Thelonious Monk biography
summary: She describes the Monk biography as a major challenge; Rowe mentions the Great Day in Harlem story and they agree Monk knew his own worth.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Yeah. Especially since so many people are dead who knew him and knew him well. So it’s a major challenge in a lot of ways. I think he was a grouch. I keep that in mind, I’ve got a certain theme in mind.
We’ve heard some interesting stories about him, connected with the “Great Day in Harlem” and what it took to get him to that session I guess.
It’s in the “Great Day in Harlem?”
Yes. He spent hours like deciding what to wear and finally picked on something that he knew would stand out from everybody else, and etcetera, etcetera.
Yeah, he was aware of how good he was and he was a little grouchy that people weren’t as aware as he was as early as he was aware.
